bio.short: Jayden Jones is a Texas sprinter from League City, a two-time Conference USA indoor 200m champion and a 4x100m All-American at two schools. A Health Promotion & Behavioral Sciences major, he was a 2026 Project Manager Intern at Feniex Industries.
long: Jayden Jones does his best work when titles and relay spots are on the line. At Sam Houston he won the Conference USA indoor 200m title as a freshman in 2024, defended it in 2025, and ran on a 4x100m that reached the NCAA Championships and earned Second Team All-America honors. After transferring to Texas he opened his first outdoor season by winning both the 100m and the 200m at the UTSA Invitational. He then helped the Longhorns' 4x100m qualify for nationals and earn Second Team All-America honors again in 2026.

Jones grew up in League City, between Houston and Galveston, and sprinted for Clear Creek High School, where he reached the 2023 UIL 6A Region III 100m final. He began college at Sam Houston, earning Conference USA Freshman of the Week honors in his first indoor season, then moved to Texas, which his official bio describes as a dream school. He studies Health Promotion & Behavioral Sciences and has been named to the USTFCCCA All-Academic Team and the First-Year SEC Academic Honor Roll.

Relay sprinting is precise teamwork at full speed: four runners, three exchanges and no room for a missed signal. Jones has earned All-America honors on relays at two schools by getting those details right. As a 2026 Project Manager Intern at Feniex Industries, the Austin manufacturer of emergency-vehicle lighting and electronics, he brought that mindset to coordinating tasks between teams, tracking schedules and keeping information moving cleanly from one group to the next. His studies in health promotion add an understanding of how people build habits and change routines.
